claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC alloy.
Equiatomic disordered-BCC NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo alloy has limited room-temperature plasticity.
Partially replacing Mo with additional Nb will reduce the alloy's overall electronegativity difference.
Reducing the electronegativity difference will decrease bond directionality in the alloy.
Reducing the electronegativity difference will decrease local lattice distortion.
Directional bonding and local lattice distortions in equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo restrict dislocation motion and contribute to brittleness.
Less directional bonding and lower local lattice distortion will facilitate dislocation motion and improve plastic deformability.
The Nb-enriched, Mo-reduced alloy will retain substantial solid-solution strengthening from its refractory elements.
The modified alloy will have greater room-temperature compressive plastic strain to failure than the equiatomic baseline.
The modified alloy will retain a room-temperature compressive yield strength comparable to the baseline value of 1719 MPa.
The proposed benefit is expected under room-temperature compressive loading when Mo reduction remains within a range that does not undermine solid-solution strengthening.
Excessive reduction of Mo may lower the alloy's strength.
